For what it's worth, I'm kind of excited to see it as a movie. The game was had a nice little story, and I wouldn't mind at all seeing it done up a little... "bigger."

All this means is that it's going to be the biggest letdown of the year.

Seriously, the ending of Firewatch was fucking terrible. It spends all this time building you up and when it comes time for the payoff it's a giant "fuck you!".

I kind of agree, but kind of disagree as well. There's a lot to something being more or less a "well, that's life - sometimes the mystery isn't laid out all nice for re-examination. Sometimes, you just gotta let it go and move on to other things." Besides the fact, I felt the focus of the story was more on Henry learning how to deal with his wife, his life, his choices etc. The 'mystery' part of it almost, I dunno, got in the way? Seemed tacked on because most people wouldn't find enough fulfillment in a personal-growth story. But seeing as how it isn't the main focus, it didn't ... I want to say "deserve" to be solved.

But then again, I only played through it once, and it was when it first came out - so I could be forgetting large swaths of the game from where I'm sitting.

The thing about stories is that people are most likely to remember the ending because it was the most recent aspect of the movie they were likely to have experienced. End a movie in a spectacularly horrible fashion and that's what people will remember.

The middle of the story was decent, and it had good tension building. The dialog was excellent - often witty and peppered with well written sarcastic and sardonic humor. The problem with the story and the ending in general is that it spends so much time building you up for something bigger than the players but it winds up being painfully mundane.

Personal growth is fine, a story about personal growth is also fine. But if you're promising the audience the world during the meat of the experience, it's best not to deliver them a bag of dogshit when it's all over.

For air and friendly talk.

Took the embankment walk.

 

Traffic holding its breath,

Sky a tense diaphragm:

Dusk hung like a backcloth

That shook where a swan swam,

Tremulous as a hawk

Hanging deadly, calm.

 

A vacuum of need

Collapsed each hunting heart

But tremulously we held

As hawk and prey apart,

Preserved classic decorum,

Deployed our talk with art.

 

Our Juvenilia

Had taught us both to wait,

Not to publish feeling

And regret it all too late -

Mushroom loves already

Had puffed and burst in hate.

As a thrush linked on a hawk,

We thrilled to the March twilight

With nervous childish talk:
